original_question: Let c be the largest constant such that every one-dimensional sequence (x_n)_{n>=0} in [0,1) satisfies the star-discrepancy lower bound D_N^* >= c log N / N for infinitely many N. Can one improve the currently known bounds 0.06015... <= c <= 0.222...?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Open Problem 16: the paper asks for the optimal universal constant in the one-dimensional star-discrepancy lower bound, i.e. to improve the best known bounds for the maximal/supremal c such that every sequence in [0,1) satisfies D_N^* >= c log N / N for infinitely many N. This is exactly the narrow problem your draft is aiming at. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the main target right: it is one-dimensional, concerns the star discrepancy D_N^*, uses the correct order log N / N, requires the bound to hold for infinitely many N, and asks about the best possible universal constant over all sequences in [0,1). That matches the intent of Open Problem 16. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
missing_details: The paper relies on the standard definition of star discrepancy from the introduction; to be stand-alone, you should define D_N^* for the first N points x_1,...,x_N of an infinite sequence by D_N^* = sup_{0<=t<=1} |(1/N) #{1<=n<=N : x_n < t} - t|. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The quantifiers should be explicit: for every infinite sequence (x_n)_{n>=1} in [0,1), there exist infinitely many N in N for which the inequality holds. The paper is about infinite sequences, not an arbitrary finite point set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

To make the constant precise, it is better to define it as a supremum c^* rather than saying 'largest constant', since attainment is not part of the statement. The paper informally says 'let c be maximal', but a stand-alone formulation is sharper with a supremum definition. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

Your draft hard-codes numerical bounds as 'currently known'; that is not paper-faithful wording. In Open Problem 16 the paper simply asks to improve the best known bounds for the constant, and the surrounding context mentions Bejian's lower bound and Ostromoukhov's upper-bound example without making the open problem itself depend on a time-sensitive 'current' benchmark. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The paper's nearby context is specifically the one-dimensional star-discrepancy problem inside Section 4 ('Miscellaneous problems'); to stay narrow, the refined question should not drift to higher-dimensional discrepancy, extreme discrepancy, or special sequence classes. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

If the question is to be fully self-contained, specify that 'log' is the natural logarithm, since the paper writes the bound in logarithmic form but does not need any other ambient algebraic structure or side assumptions here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
refined_question: For an arbitrary infinite sequence omega = (x_n)_{n>=1} in [0,1), define the one-dimensional star discrepancy of its first N points by D_N^*(omega) := sup_{0<=t<=1} |(1/N) #{1<=n<=N : x_n < t} - t|. Let c^* := sup{ c > 0 : for every such sequence omega, one has N D_N^*(omega) >= c log N for infinitely many N }, where log denotes the natural logarithm. Can one improve the best known lower and upper bounds for c^*? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: Open Problem 16 in Section 4 asks for the optimal one-dimensional star-discrepancy constant and explicitly says to improve the best known bounds. The notation D_N^* and the meaning of star discrepancy come from the introduction. Your draft is close, but it needs the exact discrepancy definition, the full quantifier order, and a supremum-style definition of the constant to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. Also, the paper does not contain Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the relevant labeled target here is Open Problem 16. The chapter metadata lists the published version on pp. 171-190. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
